## FULMINANT CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

## Discontinue any antibiotics if possible.

## Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic therapy is still needed.

## Discontinue antacid therapy if possible.

## There are no available data supporting the use of fidaxomicin for treatment of fulminant CDI.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Antimicrobial therapy for CDI should be continued for 10 days. In patients being treated with antibiotics for predisposing infections, consider continuing treatment for 7 days after completion of those antibiotics. If patient is being treated for CDI recurrence, pulse taper therapy is indicated after resolution of severe disease. Refer to mild to moderate CDI treatment menu for recommendations.

Therapy:
## Inpatient

## Treatment if ileus is present

General Surgery consult is essential for ileus or megacolon. Recommend Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Disease consults for fulminant CDI. Deliver antimicrobials by intravenous, oral, and rectal routes.

Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI] <AND> vancomycin 500 mg PO q6h [M]
<AND> vancomycin enema 500 mg in 100 ml normal saline q6h [M]

**ONLY for Vancomycin NG administration**
Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI] <AND> vancomycin 500 mg NG soln q6h [M]
<AND> vancomycin enema 500 mg in 100 ml normal saline q6h [M]

## Treatment if ileus is not present

Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases consults are recommended.
Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI] <AND> vancomycin 500 mg PO q6h [M]

**ONLY for Vancomycin NG administration**
Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI] <AND> vancomycin 500 mg NG q6h [M]

## Outpatient

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS
